source.primary_manuscript: Codex Vaticanus (B/03; Vatican Library Gr. 1209, 4th c. CE ~325-350)
source.primary_manuscript_contains: Essentially complete New Testament; complete Acts
source.secondary_manuscript: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + 4th c.). Codex Bezae (D/05; 5th c.) preserves Western-text Acts.
source.early_papyri_cross_collation: P45 (Chester Beatty I; 3rd c. CE) preserves portions of Acts. The 4th-c. uncials Vaticanus + Sinaiticus remain primary for Acts 17.
source.reference_critical_apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017). Boismard-Lamouille for Western readings.
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly Koine Greek transliteration (SBL convention): polytonic-stripped lowercase Latin with diacritics for breathings (h- for rough; nothing for smooth) and Greek-specific letters (ē for eta, ō for omega, ph for phi, ch for chi, ps for psi, th for theta, rh for rho with rough breathing); ai/ei/oi/au/eu/ou diphthongs preserved; accent marks generally omitted in scholarly translit
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Bezae + P45 original codicology + the NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus + Aratus *Phaenomena* manuscript tradition for the v.28 verbatim citation.
source.fetchedFrom: SBLGNT public-domain edition (Holmes 2010) + NA28 reference + Metzger UBS Textual Commentary (2nd ed. 1994) ad loc. + Aratus *Phaenomena* (Loeb 129).
source.citation: Aland, Aland, Karavidopoulos, Martini, Metzger, eds., *Novum Testamentum Graece*, 28th ed. (Nestle-Aland, Stuttgart 2012). UBS5 = Aland et al., *The Greek New Testament*, 5th ed. (United Bible Societies 2014). Holmes, M. W., ed., *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (SBL 2010; public-domain). Jongkind, D., ed., *The Greek New Testament*, Tyndale House (Crossway 2017). Metzger, B. M., *A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament*, 2nd ed. (UBS 1994). Codex Vaticanus: Vatican Library Gr. 1209 (4th c.). Codex Sinaiticus: British Library Add. 43725 + (4th c.). Codex Bezae: Cambridge UL Nn.II.41 (5th c.). Aratus, *Phaenomena*, ed. Kidd (Cambridge 1997); cf. Loeb *Callimachus, Lycophron, Aratus* (Mair 1921). Cleanthes *Hymn to Zeus*, ed. Thom (Mohr Siebeck 2005). Epimenides fragments in Diels-Kranz *Die Fragmente der Vorsokratiker* (DK 3 B 1). Barrett ICC 1994-1998 (vol 2); Bock BECNT 2007; Bruce NICNT 1988; Conzelmann Hermeneia 1987; Fitzmyer AB 1998; Haenchen 1971; Johnson SP 1992; Keener 2012-2015 (vol 3); Pervo Hermeneia 2009; Witherington 1998; Norden, E., *Agnostos Theos* (Teubner 1913) — foundational study of the Areopagus speech; Gärtner *The Areopagus Speech and Natural Revelation* (Almqvist 1955); Levine-Brettler JANT 2017; Mussies, G., 'Pagan Sources and the Areopagus Speech' in van der Horst-Mussies *Studies on the Hellenistic Background of the New Testament* (Utrecht 1990).
source.paleography_note: The Koine Greek text is preserved in polytonic form as transmitted via SBLGNT. Acts 17 is paleographically significant for its verbatim citation of Aratus *Phaenomena* line 5 in v.28 — one of the few places where a NT text directly quotes pagan Greek literature. The early Greek manuscripts use scriptio continua. Nomina sacra appear abbreviated in the uncials.

verses.text: Διοδεύσαντες δὲ τὴν Ἀμφίπολιν καὶ τὴν Ἀπολλωνίαν ἦλθον εἰς Θεσσαλονίκην, ὅπου ἦν συναγωγὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
verses.translit: Diodeusantes de tēn Amphipolin kai tēn Apollōnian ēlthon eis Thessalonikēn, hopou ēn synagōgē tōn Ioudaiōn.
verses.notes: Via Egnatia route west: Philippi → Amphipolis → Apollonia → Thessalonica. Standard Roman milestone-distances support the Lukan itinerary. Thessalonica = capital of Macedonia province, major Jewish community.

verses.text: κατὰ δὲ τὸ εἰωθὸς τῷ Παύλῳ εἰσῆλθεν πρὸς αὐτούς, καὶ ἐπὶ σάββατα τρία διελέξατο αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν γραφῶν,
verses.translit: kata de to eiōthos tō Paulō eisēlthen pros autous, kai epi sabbata tria dielexato autois apo tōn graphōn,
verses.notes: *to eiōthos* (his custom) — Pauline mission-pattern: synagogue first. Three Sabbaths of scriptural dialogue (*dielexato* — dialectical reasoning). Cross-corpus 1 Thess 2 + 3 (Paul's own retrospective on the Thessalonian mission).

verses.text: διανοίγων καὶ παρατιθέμενος ὅτι τὸν χριστὸν ἔδει παθεῖν καὶ ἀναστῆναι ἐκ νεκρῶν, καὶ ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστός, ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὃν ἐγὼ καταγγέλλω ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: dianoigōn kai paratithemenos hoti ton christon edei pathein kai anastēnai ek nekrōn, kai hoti houtos estin ho christos, ho Iēsous hon egō katangellō hymin.
verses.notes: *dianoigōn* (opening up) — scriptural-exposition vocabulary (cf. Luke 24:32, 45). Pauline kerygma: suffering-and-rising Messiah from scripture + identification with Jesus.

verses.text: καί τινες ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐπείσθησαν καὶ προσεκληρώθησαν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Σιλᾷ, τῶν τε σεβομένων Ἑλλήνων πλῆθος πολὺ γυναικῶν τε τῶν πρώτων οὐκ ὀλίγαι.
verses.translit: kai tines ex autōn epeisthēsan kai proseklērōthēsan tō Paulō kai tō Sila, tōn te sebomenōn Hellēnōn plēthos poly gynaikōn te tōn prōtōn ouk oligai.
verses.notes: *sebomenōn Hellēnōn* (devout Greeks) — God-fearers, Gentiles attached to the synagogue without full conversion. *gynaikōn tōn prōtōn ouk oligai* (not a few prominent women) — Lukan attention to elite-women converts (cf. 16:14 Lydia).

verses.text: Ζηλώσαντες δὲ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ προσλαβόμενοι τῶν ἀγοραίων ἄνδρας τινὰς πονηροὺς καὶ ὀχλοποιήσαντες ἐθορύβουν τὴν πόλιν, καὶ ἐπιστάντες τῇ οἰκίᾳ Ἰάσονος ἐζήτουν αὐτοὺς προαγαγεῖν εἰς τὸν δῆμον·
verses.translit: Zēlōsantes de hoi Ioudaioi kai proslabomenoi tōn agoraiōn andras tinas ponērous kai ochlopoiēsantes ethorouboun tēn polin, kai epistantes tē oikia Iasonos ezētoun autous proagagein eis ton dēmon·
verses.notes: *agoraiōn* (market-loungers) — Lukan urban-low-life vocabulary. Jason's house — Pauline host (named host, possibly a relative — cf. Rom 16:21).

verses.text: μὴ εὑρόντες δὲ αὐτοὺς ἔσυρον Ἰάσονα καί τινας ἀδελφοὺς ἐπὶ τοὺς πολιτάρχας, βοῶντες ὅτι Οἱ τὴν οἰκουμένην ἀναστατώσαντες οὗτοι καὶ ἐνθάδε πάρεισιν,
verses.translit: mē heurontes de autous esyron Iasona kai tinas adelphous epi tous politarchas, boōntes hoti Hoi tēn oikoumenēn anastatōsantes houtoi kai enthade pareisin,
verses.notes: *politarchas* (city-rulers) — distinctively Thessalonian magistracy-title, attested epigraphically in Thessalonian inscriptions (cf. Horsley *New Documents Illustrating Early Christianity* 2.34) — Lukan local-color accuracy. *tēn oikoumenēn anastatōsantes* ("those who have upset the world") — famous rhetorical-charge.

verses.text: οὓς ὑποδέδεκται Ἰάσων· καὶ οὗτοι πάντες ἀπέναντι τῶν δογμάτων Καίσαρος πράσσουσι, βασιλέα ἕτερον λέγοντες εἶναι Ἰησοῦν.
verses.translit: hous hypodedektai Iasōn· kai houtoi pantes apenanti tōn dogmatōn Kaisaros prassousi, basilea heteron legontes einai Iēsoun.
verses.notes: **SEDITION-CHARGE**. *basilea heteron … Iēsoun* (another king, Jesus). *apenanti tōn dogmatōn Kaisaros* (against the decrees of Caesar) — possibly the 49 CE Claudius-edict (cf. Suetonius *Claudius* 25.4 + Acts 18:2). Political-treason framing of Pauline kerygma.

verses.text: ἐτάραξαν δὲ τὸν ὄχλον καὶ τοὺς πολιτάρχας ἀκούοντας ταῦτα,
verses.translit: etaraxan de ton ochlon kai tous politarchas akouontas tauta,
verses.notes: Crowd + politarchs alarmed.

verses.text: καὶ λαβόντες τὸ ἱκανὸν παρὰ τοῦ Ἰάσονος καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν ἀπέλυσαν αὐτούς.
verses.translit: kai labontes to hikanon para tou Iasonos kai tōn loipōn apelysan autous.
verses.notes: *labontes to hikanon* = taking surety/bail (Latin *satisdatio*). Roman legal-bond. Jason posts bond. The Thessalonian crisis is closed legally but Paul is implicitly bound not to return (cf. 1 Thess 2:18 'Satan hindered us').

verses.text: Οἱ δὲ ἀδελφοὶ εὐθέως διὰ νυκτὸς ἐξέπεμψαν τόν τε Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Σιλᾶν εἰς Βέροιαν, οἵτινες παραγενόμενοι εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀπῄεσαν.
verses.translit: Hoi de adelphoi eutheōs dia nyktos exepempsan ton te Paulon kai ton Silan eis Beroian, hoitines paragenomenoi eis tēn synagōgēn tōn Ioudaiōn apēesan.
verses.notes: Night-escape to Berea (modern Veria, ~80 km SW). Synagogue-first pattern continues.

verses.text: οὗτοι δὲ ἦσαν εὐγενέστεροι τῶν ἐν Θεσσαλονίκῃ, οἵτινες ἐδέξαντο τὸν λόγον μετὰ πάσης προθυμίας, καθ’ ἡμέραν ἀνακρίνοντες τὰς γραφὰς εἰ ἔχοι ταῦτα οὕτως.
verses.translit: houtoi de ēsan eugenesteroi tōn en Thessalonikē, hoitines edexanto ton logon meta pasēs prothymias, kath’ hēmeran anakrinontes tas graphas ei echoi tauta houtōs.
verses.notes: **FAMOUS 'NOBLE BEREANS' VERSE**. *eugenesteroi* (more noble-minded). *anakrinontes tas graphas* (examining the scriptures) — daily scriptural-verification. Cited in Protestant tradition as the locus classicus for sola scriptura epistemology.

verses.text: πολλοὶ μὲν οὖν ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐπίστευσαν, καὶ τῶν Ἑλληνίδων γυναικῶν τῶν εὐσχημόνων καὶ ἀνδρῶν οὐκ ὀλίγοι.
verses.translit: polloi men oun ex autōn episteusan, kai tōn Hellēnidōn gynaikōn tōn euschēmonōn kai andrōn ouk oligoi.
verses.notes: Many Jews + Greek aristocratic women + men converted. *euschēmonōn* (well-born / respectable). Lukan repetition of the elite-women theme.

verses.text: Ὡς δὲ ἔγνωσαν οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Θεσσαλονίκης Ἰουδαῖοι ὅτι καὶ ἐν τῇ Βεροίᾳ κατηγγέλη ὑπὸ τοῦ Παύλου ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ, ἦλθον κἀκεῖ σαλεύοντες καὶ ταράσσοντες τοὺς ὄχλους.
verses.translit: Hōs de egnōsan hoi apo tēs Thessalonikēs Ioudaioi hoti kai en tē Beroia katēngelē hypo tou Paulou ho logos tou theou, ēlthon kakei saleuontes kai tarassontes tous ochlous.
verses.notes: Thessalonian opposition pursues Paul to Berea. *saleuontes* (shaking up) + *tarassontes* (disturbing) — Lukan agitation-vocabulary.

verses.text: εὐθέως δὲ τότε τὸν Παῦλον ἐξαπέστειλαν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πορεύεσθαι ἕως ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν· ὑπέμεινάν τε ὅ τε Σιλᾶς καὶ ὁ Τιμόθεος ἐκεῖ.
verses.translit: eutheōs de tote ton Paulon exapesteilan hoi adelphoi poreuesthai heōs epi tēn thalassan· hypemeinan te ho te Silas kai ho Timotheos ekei.
verses.notes: Paul sent away alone, by sea (likely to Athens). Silas + Timothy remain in Berea — will rejoin in Athens later (v.15) or Corinth (cf. 18:5; 1 Thess 3:1-6).

verses.text: οἱ δὲ καθιστάνοντες τὸν Παῦλον ἤγαγον ἕως Ἀθηνῶν, καὶ λαβόντες ἐντολὴν πρὸς τὸν Σιλᾶν καὶ τὸν Τιμόθεον ἵνα ὡς τάχιστα ἔλθωσιν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐξῄεσαν.
verses.translit: hoi de kathistanontes ton Paulon ēgagon heōs Athēnōn, kai labontes entolēn pros ton Silan kai ton Timotheon hina hōs tachista elthōsin pros auton exēesan.
verses.notes: **PAUL ARRIVES IN ATHENS** — the cultural-philosophical capital of the Greek world. Sets up the Areopagus-speech narrative.

verses.text: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς Ἀθήναις ἐκδεχομένου αὐτοὺς τοῦ Παύλου, παρωξύνετο τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ θεωροῦντος κατείδωλον οὖσαν τὴν πόλιν.
verses.translit: En de tais Athēnais ekdechomenou autous tou Paulou, parōxyneto to pneuma autou en autō theōrountos kateidōlon ousan tēn polin.
verses.notes: *kateidōlon* (full of idols) — hapax in NT. Athens was famously dense with cult-images (cf. Pausanias *Description of Greece* 1; Pliny *NH* 36.17 — 'Athens has 3000 statues'). *parōxyneto* (was provoked) — root of *paroxysmos* (cf. 15:39).

verses.text: διελέγετο μὲν οὖν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις καὶ τοῖς σεβομένοις καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ κατὰ πᾶσαν ἡμέραν πρὸς τοὺς παρατυγχάνοντας.
verses.translit: dielegeto men oun en tē synagōgē tois Ioudaiois kai tois sebomenois kai en tē agora kata pasan hēmeran pros tous paratynchanontas.
verses.notes: Dual venue: synagogue (Jews + God-fearers) + agora (general public). The agora setting deliberately evokes **Socrates** (who taught in the Athenian Agora — Plato *Apol.* 17c). Lukan philosopher-typology.

verses.text: τινὲς δὲ καὶ τῶν Ἐπικουρείων καὶ Στοϊκῶν φιλοσόφων συνέβαλλον αὐτῷ, καί τινες ἔλεγον· Τί ἂν θέλοι ὁ σπερμολόγος οὗτος λέγειν; οἱ δέ· Ξένων δαιμονίων δοκεῖ καταγγελεὺς εἶναι· ὅτι τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ τὴν ἀνάστασιν εὐηγγελίζετο.
verses.translit: tines de kai tōn Epikoureiōn kai Stoikōn philosophōn syneballon autō, kai tines elegon· Ti an theloi ho spermologos houtos legein? hoi de· Xenōn daimoniōn dokei katangeleus einai· hoti ton Iēsoun kai tēn anastasin euēngelizeto.
verses.notes: **EPICUREANS + STOICS** — the two dominant philosophical schools of Hellenistic Athens. *spermologos* (seed-picker — derogatory term for a bird picking up seeds; metaphorically a scrap-collecting plagiarist; cf. Aristophanes *Birds* 232; Demosthenes 18.127). *xenōn daimoniōn katangeleus* (proclaimer of foreign divinities) — EXACT FORMAL CHARGE AGAINST SOCRATES (cross-corpus Plato *Apol.* 24b *theous hous hē polis nomizei ou nomizōn, hetera de daimonia kaina*; Xenophon *Mem.* 1.1.1). Lukan literary deliberation: Paul-as-Socrates typology. *tēn anastasin* (the resurrection) — the listeners may have heard this as a goddess-name ("Anastasis"), explaining the 'foreign divinities' plural.

verses.text: ἐπιλαβόμενοί τε αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν Ἄρειον Πάγον ἤγαγον λέγοντες· Δυνάμεθα γνῶναι τίς ἡ καινὴ αὕτη ἡ ὑπὸ σοῦ λαλουμένη διδαχή;
verses.translit: epilabomenoi te autou epi ton Areion Pagon ēgagon legontes· Dynametha gnōnai tis hē kainē hautē hē hypo sou laloumenē didachē?
verses.notes: **THE AREOPAGUS**. *Areios Pagos* (Hill of Ares / Mars Hill) — historic Athenian court located west of the Acropolis. Either (a) literally the hill, or (b) the council named after the hill (the Council of the Areopagus, which had jurisdiction over religion and morals in classical and Hellenistic Athens). Modern scholarship is split (Barnes 1989). The famous Socrates-trial was held before this jurisdiction by analogy.

verses.text: ξενίζοντα γάρ τινα εἰσφέρεις εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς ἡμῶν· βουλόμεθα οὖν γνῶναι τίνα θέλει ταῦτα εἶναι.
verses.translit: xenizonta gar tina eispherein eis tas akoas hēmōn· boulometha oun gnōnai tina thelei tauta einai.
verses.notes: *xenizonta* (strange / foreign) — wordplay with *xenōn daimoniōn* v.18.

verses.text: Ἀθηναῖοι δὲ πάντες καὶ οἱ ἐπιδημοῦντες ξένοι εἰς οὐδὲν ἕτερον ηὐκαίρουν ἢ λέγειν τι ἢ ἀκούειν τι καινότερον.
verses.translit: Athēnaioi de pantes kai hoi epidēmountes xenoi eis ouden heteron ēukairoun ē legein ti ē akouein ti kainoteron.
verses.notes: **LUKAN ETHNOGRAPHIC ASIDE — ATHENIAN NOVELTY-OBSESSION**. *ti kainoteron* (something newer — comparative). Echoes the classical Athenian stereotype of *neōterismos* (revolution-loving). Cross-corpus Demosthenes 4.10; Thucydides 3.38.4. Lukan literary touch.

verses.text: Σταθεὶς δὲ Παῦλος ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ Ἀρείου Πάγου ἔφη· Ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, κατὰ πάντα ὡς δεισιδαιμονεστέρους ὑμᾶς θεωρῶ·
verses.translit: Statheis de Paulos en mesō tou Areiou Pagou ephē· Andres Athēnaioi, kata panta hōs deisidaimonesterous hymas theōrō·
verses.notes: **AREOPAGUS SPEECH BEGINS**. *Andres Athēnaioi* (Men of Athens) — the standard rhetorical address used in classical Athenian forensic + deliberative oratory (Demosthenes; Lysias). *deisidaimonesterous* (more religious / more god-fearing) — DELIBERATELY AMBIGUOUS: can mean (a) positively pious (LSJ entry 1; cf. Strabo 10.3.23) or (b) superstitious (cf. Theophrastus *Char.* 16; Plutarch *De superstitione*). Pauline rhetorical captatio benevolentiae playing the ambiguity.

verses.text: διερχόμενος γὰρ καὶ ἀναθεωρῶν τὰ σεβάσματα ὑμῶν εὗρον καὶ βωμὸν ἐν ᾧ ἐπεγέγραπτο· Ἀγνώστῳ θεῷ. ὃ οὖν ἀγνοοῦντες εὐσεβεῖτε, τοῦτο ἐγὼ καταγγέλλω ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: dierchomenos gar kai anatheōrōn ta sebasmata hymōn heuron kai bōmon en hō epegegrapto· Agnōstō theō. ho oun agnoountes eusebeite, touto egō katangellō hymin.
verses.notes: **FAMOUS *AGNŌSTŌ THEŌ* VERSE — 'TO AN UNKNOWN GOD'**. The unknown-god altar reference. Pausanias *Description of Greece* 1.1.4 confirms altars *theois agnōstois* (in plural) at Phaleron (the Athenian port). Philostratus *Apoll.* 6.3.5 also mentions Athenian altars *agnōstōn theōn*. Diogenes Laertius *Lives* 1.110 attributes such altars to Epimenides the Cretan. Whether Paul or Luke had access to a singular-formula altar or generalized from plural-altars is debated (Norden 1913 thinks the speech is heavily Lukan literary-shaping). **PAULINE RHETORICAL MOVE**: identify the *agnōstos theos* with the God he proclaims — a classical *ad hominem* / *ad rem* synthesis. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: this verse is engaged in the Raëlian canon as natural-theology proof of unknown-creator awareness; preserve.

verses.text: ὁ θεὸς ὁ ποιήσας τὸν κόσμον καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ, οὗτος οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς ὑπάρχων κύριος οὐκ ἐν χειροποιήτοις ναοῖς κατοικεῖ
verses.translit: ho theos ho poiēsas ton kosmon kai panta ta en autō, houtos ouranou kai gēs hyparchōn kyrios ouk en cheiropoiētois naois katoikei
verses.notes: **CREATION-CLAIM**. *ho theos ho poiēsas ton kosmon* — Genesis-style creation-claim re-phrased for Stoic-philosophical Greek audience. *ouk en cheiropoiētois naois katoikei* (does not dwell in temples made with hands) — cross-corpus Isa 66:1-2; 1 Kgs 8:27; 2 Chr 6:18; cf. Acts 7:48 (Stephen's speech, same critique). **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward Raëlian readings of *ouranou kai gēs … kyrios* (Lord of heaven and earth) as extraterrestrial-creator claim; preserve.

verses.text: οὐδὲ ὑπὸ χειρῶν ἀνθρωπίνων θεραπεύεται προσδεόμενός τινος, αὐτὸς διδοὺς πᾶσι ζωὴν καὶ πνοὴν καὶ τὰ πάντα·
verses.translit: oude hypo cheirōn anthrōpinōn therapeuetai prosdeomenos tinos, autos didous pasi zōēn kai pnoēn kai ta panta·
verses.notes: **ANTI-CULT POLEMIC**. The deity is not served by hands as if needing anything. *autos didous pasi zōēn kai pnoēn* (himself giving to all life and breath) — cross-corpus Gen 2:7 LXX *enephysēsen … pnoēn zōēs*; Isa 42:5 LXX *didous pnoēn tō laō*. **MAJOR LENS-RISK FLAG**: the *didous pasi zōēn kai pnoēn* (giver of life and breath to all) phrase is engaged in the Raëlian canon as Elohim-as-source-of-life-on-earth claim. Acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework applies. Preserve.

verses.text: ἐποίησέν τε ἐξ ἑνὸς πᾶν ἔθνος ἀνθρώπων κατοικεῖν ἐπὶ παντὸς προσώπου τῆς γῆς, ὁρίσας προστεταγμένους καιροὺς καὶ τὰς ὁροθεσίας τῆς κατοικίας αὐτῶν,
verses.translit: epoiēsen te ex henos pan ethnos anthrōpōn katoikein epi pantos prosōpou tēs gēs, horisas prostetagmenous kairous kai tas horothesias tēs katoikias autōn,
verses.notes: **UNITY OF HUMANITY**. *ex henos* (from one [man / blood / source]) — single ancestor claim. Variant: some witnesses read *ex henos haimatos* (from one blood) — likely a 2nd-c. expansion. Cross-corpus Gen 10 (the Table of Nations); Deut 32:8 LXX (Yahweh fixing the boundaries of the nations). The deterministic-times/places framing has parallels in Stoic *pronoia* theology. **MAJOR LENS-RISK FLAG**: *epoiēsen ex henos* is a heavily engaged verse in heterodox and Raëlian readings (single-creation-event language). Preserve.

verses.text: ζητεῖν τὸν θεὸν εἰ ἄρα γε ψηλαφήσειαν αὐτὸν καὶ εὕροιεν, καί γε οὐ μακρὰν ἀπὸ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου ἡμῶν ὑπάρχοντα.
verses.translit: zētein ton theon ei ara ge psēlaphēseian auton kai heuroien, kai ge ou makran apo henos hekastou hēmōn hyparchonta.
verses.notes: **NATURAL-THEOLOGY CLAIM**. *psēlaphēseian* (grope after / feel for) — striking sensory metaphor; cross-corpus Deut 28:29 LXX. *ou makran apo henos hekastou hēmōn* (not far from each one of us) — divine immanence. Cross-corpus Stoic theology (cf. Seneca *Ep.* 41.1 *prope est a te deus, tecum est, intus est*). Lukan-Pauline bridge to v.28 quotation.

verses.text: Ἐν αὐτῷ γὰρ ζῶμεν καὶ κινούμεθα καὶ ἐσμέν, ὡς καί τινες τῶν καθ’ ὑμᾶς ποιητῶν εἰρήκασιν· Τοῦ γὰρ καὶ γένος ἐσμέν.
verses.translit: En autō gar zōmen kai kinoumetha kai esmen, hōs kai tines tōn kath’ hymas poiētōn eirēkasin· Tou gar kai genos esmen.
verses.notes: **MAJOR GREEK-PHILOSOPHICAL CROSS-CORPUS SITE — VERBATIM PAGAN CITATIONS**. TWO citations in one verse: (1) *en autō zōmen kai kinoumetha kai esmen* ('in him we live and move and have our being') — traditionally attributed to **Epimenides** of Crete (6th c. BCE), preserved in a quatrain that also appears at Titus 1:12 (the famous 'Cretans are always liars' verse — likewise from Epimenides per Clement of Alexandria *Strom.* 1.59.2; Jerome). The Epimenides attribution is uncertain; Lake-Cadbury *Beginnings of Christianity* 5.246-251 surveys the debate. (2) **VERBATIM CITATION**: *tou gar kai genos esmen* ('for we are also his offspring') — this is the EXACT WORDING of **Aratus** *Phaenomena* line 5 (3rd c. BCE; ed. Kidd 1997). The same phrase appears in **Cleanthes** *Hymn to Zeus* (likely Cleanthes is the source, Aratus the quotee). Aratus was a Cilician — Paul's home region. Pauline rhetorical sophistication: deploying the audience's own poets as evidence for the kinship-with-God claim. **MAJOR RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE**: this verse is engaged in Raëlian natural-theology as Elohim-as-source-of-life passage — the *zōmen kai kinoumetha kai esmen en autō* phrase + the *genos esmen* (we are his offspring / kin) is read as confirmation of created-by-the-Designers status. Flag for Editor; acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework MUST be applied. **EDITOR DO NOT PRE-RESOLVE** toward (a) conventional natural-theology / Christian apologetic reading, (b) Stoic-philosophical immanence reading, or (c) Raëlian Elohim-source-of-life reading. Preserve.

verses.text: γένος οὖν ὑπάρχοντες τοῦ θεοῦ οὐκ ὀφείλομεν νομίζειν χρυσῷ ἢ ἀργύρῳ ἢ λίθῳ, χαράγματι τέχνης καὶ ἐνθυμήσεως ἀνθρώπου, τὸ θεῖον εἶναι ὅμοιον.
verses.translit: genos oun hyparchontes tou theou ouk opheilomen nomizein chrysō ē argyrō ē lithō, charagmati technēs kai enthymēseōs anthrōpou, to theion einai homoion.
verses.notes: **IDOL-POLEMIC**. *to theion* (the divine — neuter; the standard Greek-philosophical abstract for deity, vs. ho theos personal). Pauline accommodation to philosophical vocabulary. Cross-corpus Isa 40:18-20; 44:9-20 (the prophetic anti-idol polemic). The *genos tou theou* premise is leveraged to argue that gods cannot be material-artifacts (since their offspring are not artifacts).

verses.text: τοὺς μὲν οὖν χρόνους τῆς ἀγνοίας ὑπεριδὼν ὁ θεὸς τὰ νῦν παραγγέλλει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις πάντας πανταχοῦ μετανοεῖν,
verses.translit: tous men oun chronous tēs agnoias hyperidōn ho theos ta nyn parangellei tois anthrōpois pantas pantachou metanoein,
verses.notes: *tous chronous tēs agnoias* (the times of ignorance) — periodization of pre-Christian Gentile religion. *metanoein* (repent) — Pauline call. Cross-corpus 14:16 (Paul at Lystra) for similar periodization.

verses.text: καθότι ἔστησεν ἡμέραν ἐν ᾗ μέλλει κρίνειν τὴν οἰκουμένην ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ ἐν ἀνδρὶ ᾧ ὥρισεν, πίστιν παρασχὼν πᾶσιν ἀναστήσας αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν.
verses.translit: kathoti estēsen hēmeran en hē mellei krinein tēn oikoumenēn en dikaiosynē en andri hō hōrisen, pistin paraschōn pasin anastēsas auton ek nekrōn.
verses.notes: **ESCHATOLOGICAL CLAIM + RESURRECTION**. *en andri hō hōrisen* (in a man whom he has determined) — striking *anēr* (man) framing (cf. 2:22 *andra apodedeigmenon*). *anastēsas auton ek nekrōn* (having raised him from the dead) — resurrection as evidentiary proof. This is the kerygmatic-climax of the Areopagus speech, which produces the v.32 mocking response.

verses.text: ἀκούσαντες δὲ ἀνάστασιν νεκρῶν οἱ μὲν ἐχλεύαζον οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Ἀκουσόμεθά σου περὶ τούτου καὶ πάλιν.
verses.translit: akousantes de anastasin nekrōn hoi men echleuazon hoi de eipan· Akousometha sou peri toutou kai palin.
verses.notes: **ATHENIAN REJECTION**. *echleuazon* (mocked / scoffed) — the resurrection-claim is what produces the philosophical-mockery. Pivotal scholarly observation: classical Greek philosophy could accommodate immortality-of-soul (Platonic) but not bodily-resurrection. Cross-corpus 1 Cor 15:12-19 (Pauline resurrection-defense).

verses.text: οὕτως ὁ Παῦλος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: houtōs ho Paulos exēlthen ek mesou autōn.
verses.notes: Paul departs.

verses.text: τινὲς δὲ ἄνδρες κολληθέντες αὐτῷ ἐπίστευσαν, ἐν οἷς καὶ Διονύσιος ὁ Ἀρεοπαγίτης καὶ γυνὴ ὀνόματι Δάμαρις καὶ ἕτεροι σὺν αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: tines de andres kollēthentes autō episteusan, en hois kai Dionysios ho Areopagitēs kai gynē onomati Damaris kai heteroi syn autois.
verses.notes: **ATHENIAN CONVERTS**. *Dionysios ho Areopagitēs* — Dionysius the Areopagite (a member of the Areopagus council); 5th-c. Christian Neo-Platonic mystical theology corpus (Pseudo-Dionysius) is wrongly attributed to him. *Damaris* — only Lukan reference; possibly a foreign-resident metoikos given the female-name-only without male attachment. The Athens mission yields a small but elite convert-group; no church planting is narrated. Chapter ends.
